items: Ducrest Partners ("the Firm," "we," "us," or "our") is a legal practice offering advisory and transactional services across several commercial laws in Nigeria. We are committed to protecting the privacy and personal data of visitors to our website (the "Site"), prospective clients, and clients, in accordance with the Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 ("NDPA") and the General Application and Implementation Directive (GAID) 2025
This Privacy Policy explains what personal data we collect, how we use it, who we share it with, and the rights available to you as a data subject.
We may collect the following categories of personal data:
Information you provide directly: name, email address, phone number, company or organisation, and the content of any message submitted through a contact form, email, or scheduling request.

Client and engagement information: where you engage us for legal services, information necessary to open a file, perform conflict checks, and provide advisory or transactional services, including information relevant to entertainment contracts, intellectual property matters, digital asset transactions, or dispute resolution proceedings.
Technical information: IP address, browser type, device information, pages visited, and referring URLs, collected automatically through standard web analytics and, where applicable, cookies.

Information from third parties: where relevant to an engagement (for example, counterparties, regulators, or public registries), we may receive information about you from third parties in the course of advising a client.
We use personal data for purposes including:
Responding to enquiries and scheduling consultations;
Performing conflict-of-interest checks before accepting an engagement;
Delivering legal advisory and transactional services to clients;
Complying with our regulatory, ethical, and statutory obligations, including anti-money laundering and know-your-client requirements where applicable;
Improving and maintaining the Site;
Sending updates about the Firm's services, insights, or events, where you have opted in to receive them.

Where the NDPA/GAID requires a lawful basis, we rely on one or more of the following: your consent, the necessity of processing to perform a contract or take pre-contractual steps at your request, compliance with a legal obligation, or our legitimate interests in operating and promoting the Firm, provided those interests do not override your rights.
We do not sell personal data. We may share information with:
Professional advisers, co-counsel, or correspondent firms engaged to assist with a matter;
Service providers who support our operations (for example, IT hosting, email, and scheduling platforms), under confidentiality obligations;
Regulators, courts, or governmental authorities where required by law or in connection with a legal proceeding;
Successors in the event of a merger, restructuring, or transfer of the Firm's practice, subject to equivalent confidentiality protections.

We retain personal data for as long as necessary to fulfil the purposes described in this Policy, including to satisfy professional conduct, statutory limitation periods, and record-keeping obligations applicable to legal practitioners in Nigeria. Where data is no longer required, we take reasonable steps to securely delete or anonymise it.

We implement reasonable technical and organisational measures to protect personal data against unauthorised access, loss, misuse, or alteration, consistent with the security requirements under the NDPA/GAID.
Subject to applicable law, you may have the right to:
Request access to the personal data we hold about you;
Request correction of inaccurate or incomplete data;
Request deletion of your data, subject to our legal and professional retention obligations;
Object to or restrict certain processing;
Withdraw consent, where processing is based on consent, without affecting the lawfulness of processing before withdrawal;
Lodge a complaint with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission ("NDPC").
To exercise any of these rights, please contact us using the details in Section 11.

The Site may use cookies or similar technologies to support functionality and analytics. You can control cookie preferences through your browser settings; disabling cookies may affect certain features of the Site.
Submitting information through the Site, including via a contact form or email, does not create an attorney-client relationship with Ducrest Partners. Please see our Disclaimer for further detail.
For questions about this Privacy Policy or to exercise your data protection rights, please contact:
